senses.definition: Representing a loud noise or heavy impact.
examples: The wind knocked the tree over last night. Bam! It nearly scared me to death.

quotes.text: We all looked up from the maps, silent, and listened to the hurried footsteps in the entryway. They padded up the red carpet, bam-bam-bam, and across the landing and then up the next flight at a gallop, bam-bam-bam.
quotes.reference: 2007, Joe Biden, Promises to Keep, New York: Random House, published 2008, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 266:

senses.definition: Representing a sudden or abrupt occurrence.
examples: She said she dumped him. Now — bam! — they're back together.

senses.definition: (slang, archaic) An imposition; a cheat; a hoax.

quotes.text: To relieve the tedium he kept plying them with all manner of bams.
quotes.reference: 1844, John Wilson, Essay on the Genius, and Character of Burns:

senses.definition: (slang, archaic) To impose on (someone) by a falsehood; to cheat.
examples: I’ll break a lamp, bully a constable, bam a justice, or bilk a boxkeeper with any man in the liberties of Westminster.

quotes.text: This is some conspiracy, I suppose, to bam, to chouse me out of my money

senses.definition: (slang, archaic) To jeer or make fun of.
